timeline.event: Stephanie Kwolek at DuPont discovered the liquid-crystalline para-aramid solutions from which Kevlar fiber was later spun.
DuPont announced Kevlar EXO in April as a new aramid fiber platform made at Spruance, Virginia.
DuPont agreed on 29 August to sell its Aramids business, which had about 1,900 employees and five manufacturing sites, to Arclin.
Arclin completed the roughly 1.8 billion dollar acquisition on 1 April, with DuPont retaining a stake of about 16% in Arclin.

timeline.event: DSM invented and patented the gel-spinning process for ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene fiber (Smith and Lemstra).
Commercial Dyneema fiber production began at Heerlen, the Netherlands.
Avient completed its purchase of DSM Protective Materials, the Dyneema business, on 1 September for about 1.4 billion dollars net of cash.

timeline.event: A Zimmer AG author described the production of a lyocell fiber containing seaweed and its silver-loaded antimicrobial variant.
Dermatologists reported antifungal and antibacterial activity of the silver-loaded seaweed fiber in laboratory tests.
A randomized, single-blinded study in 37 people with atopic dermatitis reported less Staphylococcus aureus colonization with the silver-loaded fiber than with cotton over 8 weeks.

timeline.event: A sports-science study used COOLMAX as a profiled cross-section polyester benchmark and attributed it to INVISTA of Wichita, Kansas.
The LYCRA Company and ITOCHU introduced COOLMAX EcoMade fiber made from 100% textile waste, recovered by depolymerization.
The LYCRA Company, which presents the COOLMAX brand, emerged from Chapter 11 on 20 May.
